paper.title_en: Self-consistency of the generalized uncertainty principle modified membrane model and its consistency with the weak cosmic censorship condition in Reissner-Nordström-de Sitter black holes
paper.abstract_en: We investigate four-dimensional Reissner-Nordström-de Sitter (RN-dS) black holes within the generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) modified membrane model. The conventional membrane model is plagued by an unnatural cutoff that might lack fundamental physical meaning. In this work, we resolve this issue by introducing a natural, quantum-gravity-motivated cutoff derived from the minimal length predicted by the GUP. Using the membrane paradigm, we compute the free energy and entropy of quantum fields confined near the horizon and enforce normalization to the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy. We analytically solve the membrane thickness and show that its positive definiteness is strictly equivalent to the positivity of surface gravity at the event horizon, which in turn supports the validity of WCCC. The model also naturally breaks down at the Planck scale, consistent with the expected limit of semiclassical gravity. Our results reveal a consistent link between quantum-gravity-motivated horizon thermodynamics and the non-degeneracy condition underlying cosmic censorship.
